Use the Claw Me source at https://github.com/clawdotme/plugin in templates/inventory-snapshot/index.html and templates/_shared/tailwind/README.md. Use semantic responsive HTML, working section links, and useful native details/summary interactions. No scripts, forms, tracking, or embedded frames in the static Page. PDF export is separate from Page publishing unless the current platform explicitly supports it.

exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: An inventory snapshot with counted stock, reorder points, and reconciliation notes.
exampleAnswers.Working context: The fictional workshop store counts consumables before each monthly event. Quantities below are sample units from a manual stocktake, with no live warehouse connection.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Item: A5 notebooks · On hand: 18 · Reorder point: 20 · Unit: Each
Item: Black pens · On hand: 42 · Reorder point: 30 · Unit: Each
Item: Name badges · On hand: 26 · Reorder point: 25 · Unit: Each
Item: Paper rolls · On hand: 4 · Reorder point: 3 · Unit: Roll
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Order decision: Notebooks are below the chosen reorder point. Confirm next month’s attendance and the supplier’s pack size before placing an order. Pens, badges, and paper remain above their sample thresholds.
Count with context: Record damaged or reserved stock separately from usable stock. If two counts disagree, reconcile the shelf location and unit before adjusting the total.
Keep the record current: Name the person who completed the count and the time of the snapshot. A purchase or event after that time changes available stock and should trigger an update.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: ledger layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
